key_insight: A deep learning model can screen for chronic kidney disease using standard parasternal long-axis echocardiography videos.
clinical_relevance: If validated in practice, this approach could help flag previously undiagnosed CKD during routine cardiac imaging and support earlier follow-up.
method: Trained on 325,377 PLAX echo videos from 62,818 patients at Cedars-Sinai.
Externally validated in 2,224 patients at Stanford and 41,611 patients at Kaiser Permanente Northern California.
Used deep learning to predict any-stage CKD from echocardiography videos.
evidence_signal: The model achieved AUC 0.756 in the Cedars-Sinai held-out test cohort and showed similar external performance at Stanford (0.719) and Kaiser Permanente Northern California (0.718).
watch_item: Performance was strong but not definitive, so real-world deployment would need prospective validation and attention to site-specific workflow and population differences.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Enabled Screening of Chronic Kidney Disease from Echocardiography
